reason: The turning sensor cells fit at the base of the fluid-filled loops, where fluid movement bends their hairs.
expectation: This should build the sensors that detect changes in turning.

alternatives.reason: The pictures also show how to build the tilt sensors, so either project could come first.

effect: The fluid-filled loops and sensor cells form turning sensors; fluid movement bends the flap and changes a nerve signal.
reaction: The picture makes the connection between movement and the signal clear.
reason: The picture shows the mineral weights resting on the jelly above the tilt sensor cells, so they look like matching parts.
expectation: The weights and cells should form the tilt sensors.

effect: The weighted sensors respond to tilt and changes in straight-line movement. Both sensor types are now built, so they need connecting.
reaction: The shifting weighted layer makes their job clearer.
reason: Balance nerves are pictured leading from both sensor types to the brain, so I’ll start connecting them to the turning sensors.
expectation: The turning sensors should connect to the nerves leading to the brain.

alternatives.reason: The balance nerves also connect to the weighted sensors.

effect: The two sensor types had to be joined into balance organs before connecting the nerves.
reaction: I was surprised they needed to be combined first; the compatibility hint made that clear.
reason: The balance nerves lead from both sensor types to the brain, so they should connect to the assembled organs.
expectation: The balance organs should gain a nerve connection to the brain.

effect: The assembled balance organs now have nerve routes into the brain.
reason: The eye and posture nerve routes lead from the brain toward the muscles that keep the eyes and body steady, so I'll try connecting them to the balance organs.
expectation: The balance signals should connect to routes controlling eye and posture muscles.

alternatives.reason: The organs may need to join the body before the movement routes can be connected.

effect: The balance sensors now connect through the brain and spinal cord to eye and posture muscles.
reason: The movement connections need to join the existing body to complete the goal.
expectation: The body should gain connected balance sensors and movement routes.

effect: The completed body model shows how balance signals help steady the eyes and posture, alongside vision and signals from muscles and joints.
reaction: The eyes turning opposite the head made the purpose of the connections clearer.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the balance system to the body was most worthwhile: the final picture showed what the sensors actually help the body do.

leastWorthwhile.text: Connecting the nerves and then the movement routes felt a little repetitive, even though both connections made sense.

surprise.text: I expected to connect the turning sensors directly to the nerves, but the hint showed that the two sensor types had to be joined first.

arbitrary.text: That prerequisite felt somewhat arbitrary: the pictures showed nerves reaching both sensors, but did not make it clear why the sensors had to be combined first.

continue.text: I would probably continue for another chapter to see how another body system connects to familiar actions, although the repeated connection steps were less interesting than the final demonstration.
